reference.quote: What the %b indicator does is quantify or display where price is in relation to the bands.

draw.today: 10 'bollinger percent' labels (x 340.1-1077.6, y 93.6-419.2) at price while the %B pane is drawn below. That pane also puts %B and bandwidth on one auto scale (indicator_series.rs:437-467), so the 1 and 0 levels sit on a scale neither series fills -- the pane and the labels are both wrong, differently.
draw.canonical: %B in its own pane with levels at 1 and 0, and the bandwidth on its own scale if drawn at all -- 'what the %b indicator does is quantify or display where price is in relation to the bands'.

fires.our_rule: %B(20,2) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when %B crosses 1 or 0 (indicator_signals.rs:212-214, n > 21)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots %B continuously against its 0/1 levels and marks no band break; the line crossing 1 or 0 is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: pctb = (close - lower) / (upper - lower) => signal when pctb crosses 1 or 0

warmup.before: bands exist from bar 20; the detector requires n > 21

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Average True Range (ATR)
reference.quote: The way to interpret the Average True Range is that the higher the ATR value, then the higher the level of volatility.

draw.today: 2 'atr family' labels (x 696-747.4, y 52.4-136.9) at price while the 23-line ATR ribbon is drawn below. The ribbon's expansion is the indicator and it is already visible; two words at price add nothing to it.
draw.canonical: the ATR ribbon in its own pane, auto-scaled, fast-to-slow gradient -- our composition of the reference's single ATR line, which establishes the pane and the units.

fires.our_rule: ATR(2)..ATR(24) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when the family mean exceeds 1.5x its own 20-bar mean (indicator_signals.rs:581, n > 60)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots one ATR continuously in its own pane and marks no expansion event; the family expansion is ours

rule_as_data.rule: for p in 2..=24: atr[p] = ATR(p) => signal when mean(atr[p]) > 1.5 * mean(mean(atr[p]), 20)

warmup.before: ATR(24) exists from bar 24; the family-mean detector requires n > 60

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Average True Range (ATR)
reference.quote: The way to interpret the Average True Range is that the higher the ATR value, then the higher the level of volatility.

draw.today: 2 'atr' labels (x 696-751.7, y 52.4-234.5) at price while the ATR(14) pane is drawn below. A volatility in price units is being announced at a price.
draw.canonical: one ATR line in its own pane, auto-scaled in the instrument's units, no levels -- 'the higher the ATR value, then the higher the level of volatility'.

fires.our_rule: ATR(14) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it exceeds 1.5x its 20-bar mean (indicator_signals.rs:618, n > 36)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots ATR continuously in its own pane and marks no expansion event; the line's rise is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: atr = ATR(14) => signal when atr > 1.5 * mean(atr, 20)

warmup.before: ATR(14) exists from bar 14; the detector requires n > 36

reference.quote: Bollinger Bands consist of a band of three lines: a middle simple moving average, and upper and lower bands set two standard deviations away from the middle line.

draw.today: 50 'bollinger' labels (x 265.1-1071.1, y 67.9-486.1) across the price frame while the three-band overlay is drawn on the same frame. Two independent drawings of one indicator: the correct band and 50 words where it already is.
draw.canonical: three lines -- the middle SMA(20) and upper/lower at two standard deviations -- on the price plot; 'Bollinger Bands consist of a band of three lines', and the reference marks no word at the bar.

fires.our_rule: SMA(20) +/- 2 sigma is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when close is outside the band (indicator_signals.rs:212-214, n > 21)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws the bands continuously and marks no breakout; price beyond the band is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: mid = SMA(close, 20); sd = stdev(close, 20); up = mid + 2*sd; lo = mid - 2*sd => signal when close > up or close < lo

warmup.before: bands exist from bar 20; the detector requires n > 21
